newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: China gets $70 million for marine aquaculture.
newsitem.headline: China gets $70 million for marine aquaculture.

text.p: The Asian Development Bank (ADB) said on Tuesday it had approved a $70 million loan to promote marine aquaculture as an alternative livelihood in China's coastal areas.

The Manila-based multilateral financing institution said the loan was to partly fund projects which would help fishermen to switch from fishing to the more profitable marine aquaculture and aquatic processing ventures.
"These will absorb 10,000 full-time and 8,000 part-time workers and it is hoped that the ventures will be successful enough to encourage many more to follow suit," the bank said in a statement.
Fishing in the coastal areas has depleted fish resources, while rapid economic growth is increasingly polluting the water.
An $810,000 technical assistance grant was also approved to prepare a long-term coastal resources management and development plan in northern China.
The loan was sourced from the bank's ordinary capital resources which carries a 6.82 percent interest rate, adjustable every six months.
China's Ministry of Agriculture, the executing agency, has 15 years to repay the loan, including a five-year grace period.
